meta.title: 3D Bioprinting of Neurovascular Tissue Modeling with Collagen-Based Low-Viscosity Composites.

extracted_by: Claude (Claude Code session), pending human review
summary: A very low-viscosity alginate/collagen bioink was printed into a gelatin support bath at ~10 µm resolution to build neurovascular unit models. Partial alginate lysis softened the gel to about 1 kPa, close to brain.

formulations.crosslinking: Ca2+ from support bath, then alginate lysis
formulations.stiffness_note: after lysis (~1 kPa); A5 before lysis 1.96 kPa
formulations.review_notes: Cell types and sources not fully captured from the text.
formulations.name: 0.5% alginate + 0.1% collagen (A5C1) in gelatin bath
formulations.composition_detail: 0.5% w/v alginate + 0.1% w/v collagen; support bath 4.5% gelatin + 0.2% CaCl2
formulations.key_outcome: Low-viscosity ink printed at ~10 µm resolution and softened to brain-like ~1 kPa after lysis.

evidence.quote: The group with 0.5% [w/v] sodium alginate/ 0.1% [w/v] collagen (A5C1) was set to be the experimental/testing group
the lysis processing can decrease the hydrogels’ modulus to ≈1 kPa
A syringe‐based extrusion printer was custom‐designed and produced.
